title: Privacy policy
summary: Draft of the full privacy information for the site, web app, extension, Account, purchase and support. Controller, legal bases and provider contracts are placeholders.
paragraphs: This is a legal-content draft, version draft-2026-11-20.1. It is not an approved privacy notice. Bracketed values and the words “placeholder” and “to be confirmed” mark facts that only the owner or a legal reviewer can supply. No provider is named as final before its contract is signed.

Controller: [legal name, address and privacy contact of the controller, see the legal notice]. Data protection officer: [name and contact, or a statement that none is required]. Competent supervisory authority: [authority].

Scope. This text covers the information site, the web app, the browser extension, the Account, the purchase of a Pro Plan or Check pack, and support. Verification, structuring and import use data sources that are named below.

Information site. It has no analytics, third-party embeds, remote fonts, sign-in or contact form, sets no cookies and does not save the language or search queries. Language is selected by URL and documentation search runs in the browser. The hosting provider necessarily receives network requests and may process the visitor’s IP address in access and security logs. [Provider, location, log content, retention period and processor terms to be confirmed.]

Guest use of the web app. A Guest needs no Account. The web app saves Preferences (language, citation style, appearance) in its own browser storage. Text submitted for a Check is processed for that Check. Without History, no stored text remains after at most 24 hours.

Account. For an Account the service stores the e-mail address, which is also the sign-in credential: it sends a one-time code by e-mail, and the code appears only in the message body. A signed-in browser holds a session in a host-scoped Secure HttpOnly cookie. The service stores Quota, Orders, consent records, DPA records and, if used, History. The cookie is needed for sign-in and is not used for tracking. [Legal basis, for example performance of the contract, to be assigned by the reviewer.]

Browser extension. The extension keeps a session credential in extension-local storage and holds a selection in memory for at most 30 seconds. The Firefox manifest declares authentication information, personally identifying information and website content. [Align this paragraph with the final manifest declarations before publication.]

References and data sources. To verify a Reference the server queries independent data sources on the user’s behalf. They receive titles, author names, years, identifiers and, for books, ISBNs: OpenAlex and Crossref (United States), Europe PMC (EMBL-EBI, United Kingdom), Semantic Scholar (United States), arXiv and doi.org (identifiers only), Open Library and Google Books (United States). For a web reference, the server fetches the cited address and may ask the Internet Archive (United States) for a snapshot. These recipients are independent and are not processors. They see the request from the service’s server address, not from the user’s. [Transfer safeguards and terms per recipient to be recorded by the reviewer.]

AI extraction. In paid Plans, AI extraction sends the text of References, and optionally the surrounding running text, to an AI provider. The text is user-supplied and can contain personal data. The requirements are: processing in the EU, no use for training, no storage by the provider. [AI provider: placeholder until the selection is final and its contract states these requirements in writing.]

Hosting and operations. The programs and their database run at [Scalingo, Paris, France, placeholder]. Encrypted backups are stored at [Scaleway Object Storage, Paris, France, placeholder]. Transactional e-mails are sent through [Scaleway Transactional Email, France, placeholder]. Operational telemetry without content goes to [Scaleway Cockpit, France, placeholder], and availability probes to [Better Stack, location to be confirmed]. A cold fallback site at [Clever Cloud, Paris] holds nothing while idle. Abuse-limiter counters are kept for at most 24 hours and security events for 30 days.

Backups. Encrypted database exports are made every six hours and locked against deletion for 312 hours. History and Account data stay in backups for at most 14 days. A deletion request therefore reaches the live data at once but cannot change a locked export before it expires. [Whether this is acceptable under Art. 17 GDPR is a question for the reviewer.]

Purchase. Payments are handled by [Stripe, placeholder]. Card data goes to the payment provider only and is not stored by the service. The payment provider receives name, e-mail address, billing address and, if given, VAT ID. [E-invoicing integration: placeholder until selected.] Invoices and their data are kept for 8 years, including after Account deletion, because of statutory retention duties. Order confirmations and invoices are sent by the service itself.

Support. [Mailbox provider, placeholder.] Support conversations are deleted 12 months after their last message, and specific billing or legal evidence follows the retention allocation above. Please do not send References or private documents with a support request.

Retention overview. Guest text without History: at most 24 hours. History: 30 days (Free) or 90 days (paid Plans). Abuse counters: at most 24 hours. Security events: 30 days. Backups: see above. Billing data and invoices: 8 years. Support: 12 months after the last message. Account data: until deletion by the user.

Rights. Users may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, data portability and object to processing, may withdraw a given consent at any time and may complain to a supervisory authority. In the web app, an Account and its History can be deleted by the user. [Contact channel for requests, to be supplied.]

Third-country transfers. Some recipients above are located in the United States and the United Kingdom. [The transfer mechanism for each recipient is to be recorded by the reviewer. None is claimed here.]
